## What

`@papercusp/sync` exposes an eager-mutation seam — `useSyncMutate(path, restFallback)` (`libs/generic/sync/src/SyncContext.ts`). Its docstring promises that the mutator "runs OPTIMISTICALLY through the Zero client (instant local apply, then server reconcile / rollback)." That is true **only on the WebSocket transport**, where a Zero client exists:

```ts
// SyncContext.ts — resolveMutator returns the Zero custom-mutator if one is
// registered; otherwise the call takes restFallback (a plain fetch).
const fn = resolveMutator(mutate, path);
if (fn) return (await fn(args)) as R;   // optimistic — WS/Zero only
return restFallback(args);              // REST — every other transport
```

Two facts make that optimistic path **dead on the shipping target**:

1. **Zero is retired** (`CLAUDE.md`, `libs/zero-harness`). No new Zero mutators are registered, so `resolveMutator` returns `null`.
2. **The desktop ships on SSE**, not WebSocket — browser WS is a dev fallback (`apps/operator/providers/HarnessSyncProvider.tsx`). With no Zero client, `useSyncMutate` deterministically takes `restFallback`.

So on the desktop, `useSyncMutate` is **behaviour-identical to a bare `fetch`** — the write round-trips and the UI only updates when the server's `notifySyncInvalidate` pushes the new rows back over SSE. There is no free optimistic apply.

## Why it bites

A mutation wired through `useSyncMutate` (or a raw POST) **feels laggy**: the control doesn't reflect the change until the round-trip completes. This reads as "is it polling?" — it isn't; it's just the absence of optimism. Reaching for `useSyncMutate` "to get optimism for free" does **not** fix it on the desktop.

## Fix — hand-roll optimism in the hook

Apply the predicted state locally for instant feedback, then reconcile with the server's authoritative response (or roll back on failure). The SSE invalidation still refreshes any derived data afterward.

```ts
const prev = state;
if (optimistic) setState(optimistic);          // instant
try {
  const res = await fetch(url, { method: 'POST', body });
  const j = await res.json();
  if (!res.ok || !j.ok) throw new Error(j.error);
  setState(j.value ?? fallback);                // reconcile with server truth
} catch (e) {
  if (optimistic) setState(prev);               // roll back
  toast.error(...);
}
```

Reference implementation: `apps/operator-vite/src/components/adv/use-account-override.ts` (the owner's session-now Force/Exclude account override — the levers flip instantly, reconcile on the POST response, roll back on error). Pin it with a tiny render-a-harness test that holds the POST open to observe the optimistic window and asserts rollback on failure (`use-account-override.test.tsx`).

A real "library-level optimism on the post-Zero transports" layer would be its own project; until then, optimism is the call site's job.
